Change Request: Tiered tests: make the checks before a pull request faster without weakening the gate. (1) Measure first: run the full suite with --durations and record where the time goes. (2) A quick local tier (compile + the tests of the changed area + a small core: api smoke, fresh database, security, release gate / integrity) for building and before opening a PR; (3) mark the slow tests (migrations from older releases, staging / restore, records archive) so a quick run can skip them; (4) run the suite in parallel (pytest-xdist, dev-only) if the measurement shows the tests are independent; (5) cache the older-release databases the migrations test builds (they never change for a given commit). The full suite stays the required check in CI on every pull request, and is run locally only when a change touches migrations, release controls or security.
Context / Rationale: Requested by N. Wrana 2026-10-23: the full local suite takes 13 to 16 minutes per change (about 710 tests in 56 files; 43 files boot their own server, the migrations test builds and upgrades a database from each of 55 older releases every run). CI takes about 5 to 6 minutes on Linux. The last CI-only failures (KW-62, KW-66, KW-68) were Linux versus Windows differences that a full local run does not catch, so CI is the real gate. Not measured yet: the speed-ups are proposals until a --durations run shows the slowest tests.
Acceptance Criteria: A timings report (--durations) is recorded; a documented quick tier that runs in about 3 minutes or less locally; slow tests marked and skippable; the full suite still runs unchanged in CI as the required check and before any release; if parallel runs are adopted, the suite passes repeatedly in parallel and in CI with no flaky failures; legacy-commit upgrade checks still run in CI; CLAUDE.md and docs/release-guide.md describe the tiers and when to use each.

(1) Write the latest hash of the release_events chain, and the row counts of the append-only logs, into every nightly backup manifest and into the SharePoint records archive, so a later rewrite of the database shows up against an external record. (2) Show a clear warning to administrators and Quality Managers when 'Verify audit trail' fails or has not been run for a set time (today a broken chain blocks nothing). (3) Put the actions that are not hash-chained today under the same protection or an equivalent append-only record: shipments and their cancellations, disposals, consumable ledger adjustments and counts, password resets and role changes. (4) Update docs/data-integrity-statement.md to say what is and is not tamper-evident.
Context / Rationale: Hardening review of 2026-10-24, finding R-19 (partly fixed in batch 6). The chain is an unkeyed SHA-256: anyone with write access to the database file can recompute it, there is no external anchor, and several record types are outside it. Release, CoA and recall records are what auditors and customers rely on. A change to an audit control needs a Quality Manager note (QM-001) and an update of the data-integrity statement.

Change Request: Declare foreign keys for the *_id columns that have none, so the database itself refuses a row that points at something that does not exist. SQLite cannot add a foreign key to an existing table, so each affected table must be rebuilt (create new, copy, check, swap) inside the existing one-transaction migration with a pre-migration snapshot. Start with an inventory of the columns and the tables that hold real data, then rebuild in small steps with a check that no row is orphaned before the foreign key is added.
Context / Rationale: Hardening review of 2026-10-24, finding R-31 (partly fixed in batch 7: status triggers and non-negative quantities exist; many *_id columns still have no foreign key). Today only code stops a bad link. Every new table gets its foreign-key columns indexed automatically, but the missing declarations remain on older tables. Needs care because the live database now holds real production data from go-live.
Acceptance Criteria: A list of every *_id column without a foreign key and the decision for each (add, or leave and why). Each added key is covered by a test that tries to insert an orphan.
